title: The J League Bodyguard
subtitle_source: subs_resolved/0907.txt (489 dialogue lines, full transcript read)
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Ran, Ayumi, Genta, Mitsuhiko) omitted by convention; Kogoro Mouri is kept as he is the story's actual poisoning victim, not just narrator. case_type corrected from the old file's 'attempted_murder' to 'attempted_poisoning' (sabotage/doping): the transcript explicitly states the substance (rhubarb, aloe, senna, bisacodyl) was 'just laxatives' and 'won't kill him', and Inspector-adjacent dialogue notes there is 'no victim or physical evidence' in a legal sense -- this was a J-League anti-doping/match-fixing sabotage, not a murder attempt. The culprit identity (Miyamoto Risa) in the old file holds up -- she is not a red herring, she confesses on-screen. However the old file's flat 3-suspect list and vague 'unspecified' motive undersell the transcript: Tonozuka and Iwasada are written as suspicious-seeming background characters (Tonozuka in particular is repeatedly called 'a creep' by the kids) but neither is ever actually implicated by evidence or accusation, so they are reclassified here as witnesses rather than suspects. Miyamoto's real motive is added from the transcript: she was blackmailed via a loan-shark scheme (a disappeared former co-signer friend and a 'Rodriguez-sensei' loan advisor, both later revealed to be part of an illegal soccer-betting/match-fixing syndicate) into lacing Akagi's sports drink -- she then deliberately handed the tampered drink to Kogoro instead of Akagi as a silent plea for him to notice and stop the scheme, which he does.
